mediaItem.itemTitle: Jason Flom with Nick Yarris in Times of COVID
mediaItem.summaryNotes: This episode of "Wrongful Conviction with Jason Flom" features Nick Yarris, an exoneree who spent years on death row for a crime he did not commit.  The conversation centers around how Yarris's experiences in prison, particularly on death row, have equipped him to cope with the COVID-19 lockdown. Yarris discusses the importance of structure, managing anger, and finding solace in literature, specifically mentioning "The Prophet" by Khalil Gibran. He draws parallels between the psychological challenges of death row and the current global situation, emphasizing the detrimental role of ego and the importance of kindness and focusing on helping others.  The episode also briefly touches on Walter Ogrod's wrongful conviction case, for whom Yarris and Flom are advocating.  Yarris shares insights on resilience, the power of literature, and maintaining humanity in dire circumstances.

keyQuotesRaw: "I refused to give up my humanity. My kindness was so important to me..." - Nick Yarris on coping in prison and during lockdown.
"The bigger the ego, the harder it is to be in lockdown." - Nick Yarris on ego and confinement.
"Each one [book] taught me a different aspect of myself." - Nick Yarris on the importance of reading books.
"Reach out and be someone else's answered prayer. Be the uplifting moment they need, and you'll feel so much better for yourself." - Nick Yarris's advice for listeners struggling during lockdown.
"We will bring Walter home..." - Jason Flom expressing determination to exonerate Walter Ogrod.

personalNarrativeRaw: Nick Yarris shares his personal experience of being wrongly convicted and sentenced to death, and how he coped with the trauma and isolation. He emphasizes his journey from anger and bitterness to finding strength through literature and self-reflection. He highlights the transformative power of reading and the importance of maintaining kindness and humanity even in the face of injustice. His narrative is presented as a source of inspiration and practical advice for listeners dealing with the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdown. His final thoughts revolve around the power of kindness and reaching out to others to offer support.
